items.title: SynFit guides enzyme engineering by balancing several useful traits at once
items.excerpt: UC Santa Barbara (Yang Yang, HHMI) and Georgia Tech (Yunan Luo) built SynFit, an open-source AI tool that learns several enzyme traits at once from a small batch of lab data and predicts variants that balance them. Trained on an engineered cytochrome c that forges carbon-boron bonds, the variants it picked were made and tested in the lab, and many hit high yield and high selectivity together (bioRxiv preprint).

items.title: New AI tool exposes plant pathogens and the genes behind them
items.excerpt: Leiden University bioinformatician Guillermo Guerrero Egido's machine-learning tool bacLIFE compares the genomes of more than 16,000 plant-associated bacteria at once. It predicts each one's lifestyle (soil, plant-beneficial or pathogenic) and flags the genes likely behind disease-causing ability, which could help spot new crop pathogens and useful farm microbes earlier.

items.title: Dark matter-hunting satellite Euclid reveals record number of cosmic 'magnifying glasses'
items.excerpt: Euclid's first major data release (DR1) yields about 15,000 new strong-gravitational-lens candidates; before Euclid there were fewer than 1,000 confirmed lenses. In the UBC-involved four-step search, machine learning first sorts the huge dataset for likely lenses, then thousands of citizen scientists refine the AI-sorted pool, and the team aims to build an ML model that can confirm lenses without human checks. Note: AI is one stage of the pipeline, not the headline.

items.title: Chat-based AI lets users run complex alloy calculations on their own computers
items.excerpt: Empa researchers (Yang Hu et al.) built OptiMat Alloys, an AI agent framework that lets materials scientists run atomistic high-entropy-alloy simulations through a plain text chat. It is grounded in scientific knowledge and computes results on demand on the user's own computer (npj Computational Materials).

items.title: Brain scans may explain why deepfake faces appear 'hyperreal'
items.excerpt: University of Florida psychologist Natalie Ebner's team showed 126 people aged 18-89 a set of 80 real and AI-generated faces while scanning their brains. Participants rated the deepfakes as more real than the real photos, and activity in the anterior insula dropped when they viewed deepfakes. Older adults showed the strongest bias (Social Cognitive and Affective Neuroscience).

items.title: New AI model could help UN nuclear watchdog achieve near-perfect uranium enrichment assessment
items.excerpt: University of Sharjah researchers trained gradient-boosting models (XGBoost, CatBoost, LightGBM) on IAEA benchmark simulations of HPGe gamma-spectroscopy detector output. The dual-task framework predicts U-235 enrichment (XGBoost R2 = 1.0000) and classifies nuclear material types with 100% accuracy, aimed at NPT safeguards (Annals of Nuclear Energy). Note: tested on simulated data only.

items.title: AI Agents Ran a Biology Lab. Humans Popped in to Empty the Trash.
items.excerpt: Shanghai Jiao Tong University's AutoDNA is a molecular biology lab run mostly by AI agents that plan experiments, control robots and run DNA synthesis and sequencing; humans only restock supplies. It finished a full DNA write-and-read cycle in about 200 hours with expert-level precision, tuned a PCR protocol to nearly 98% yield, and encoded and decoded a message across 78 DNA strands.

history_match.title: AI agents run this automated biology lab that sequences DNA and more

items.title: Using Vibrations and AI, Future Robotic Missions Could Handle Buried Rocks Autonomously
items.excerpt: Virginia Tech's Yiyan Ruan and Erik Komendera (a former NASA Langley researcher) use AI to read surface vibrations and estimate how deep partly buried rocks go. This would let energy-limited robots on the Moon or Mars decide on their own whether to dig out an obstacle or steer around it (IEEE Sensors Journal).

items.title: New AI Models Are Turbo-Charging Protein Design
items.excerpt: GEN feature (Caroline Seydel) on AI-designed protein therapeutics moving from proof of concept to wet-lab validation and clinical trials. It notes that Anthropic's Claude Opus 4.8 designed several binders to TNF-alpha, a hard target where other models had struggled. Note: this is an industry roundup feature, not a single new paper.

items.title: New AI “copilot” helps engineers design better structures
items.excerpt: MIT researchers made topology-optimization design interactive: while the algorithm generates a structure, it shows regions to a human designer for feedback. The result is more manufacturable structures with higher buckling loads for only 15 seconds of extra design time (Communications Engineering). Note: borderline engineering, not basic science.
